title: Brownie Cookies
style: Extra rich, fudgy, and chewy cookies with the flavour of a brownie.
description: Extra rich, extra fudge-like, and extra chewy brownie cookies. For best results, use good chocolate and follow the recipe closely.

items.note: ¼ cup, natural unsweetened or dutch-process

steps: Melt the chopped chocolate in a double boiler or in the microwave in 20-second increments, stirring after each, until completely melted. Set aside to cool slightly so it doesn't melt the butter or cook the eggs.
Whisk the flour, cocoa powder, espresso powder, baking powder, and salt together and set aside.
In a large bowl using a handheld or stand mixer with a paddle attachment, beat the butter, brown sugar, and granulated sugar on medium-high speed until smooth and creamy, about 3 minutes.
Add the eggs and vanilla and beat on high for 2 full minutes. Scrape down the sides and bottom of the bowl, then beat on high for 1 more minute.
Pour in the slightly cooled melted chocolate and mix on medium-high speed for 2 full minutes.
Add the dry ingredients and beat on low speed until combined, then beat in the chocolate chips.
Preheat the oven to 177°C / 350°F and line large baking sheets with parchment paper or silicone mats.

Cover and chill the dough in the refrigerator for just 20 minutes as the oven preheats — this slightly solidifies the chocolate and butter for a nice spread. If chilling longer, let the dough sit at room temperature for 15 minutes before rolling and baking.

Roll or scoop the dough into balls, 1.5 tbsp / 35 g each (a medium cookie scoop is ideal). Place 3 inches apart on the baking sheets and bake for 12–13 minutes, until the edges appear set. The centres will be quite soft but set as the cookies cool.
Let the cookies cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
tips: Use good-quality chocolate bars rather than only chips — it makes a real difference to the fudgy texture.
Chill for exactly 20 minutes: longer makes thicker cookies that may not spread at all.
The centres should look underdone when you pull them out; they firm up as they cool.
Cookies stay fresh covered at room temperature for up to 1 week.
